chapter: Theaters, the Navy and the Singletons' partnership
title: Accompanying silent films and the effects equipment
summary: Playing for pictures was good training in timing. Zutty and Marge describe the effects he had to make, such as crashes, whistles and the steamboat whistle.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: No, I don't think you told it on the first mishap. I don't remember you telling me that. But after the Rose bud then, what did you, you had to accompany the pictures?
Well that was good playing wasn't it?
Yes. It was good, very good training. Timing and.....
But of course, you had to do a lot of Effects as well as straight drumming I take it you had to do all those noises, didn't you?
Sure. We had to imitate you know the picture. A big crash would come or something like that, I'd try to follow it, you know. Zully
I think that's why they had all those different equipment that the other drummers had never seen or heard of. Like the ratchet and all that.
Well what did you do, whistles and things?
Steam boat whistle. I'd blow that steam boat whistle, you know. Try to come out a little even there you know.
Well did you have chains to rattle?

Chains. Chains. I remember, often remember seeing a picture called The Covered Wagon, you know. That was when they first started to get into the sound affects in a big way. And they would have sort of like when they cracked the whip, you know. And then they had the chains, their horses moved off, they had chains rattling. But of course, you were all set to imitate horses hooves.
